Recognizing the wickedness of these eunuchs, our Mardochai exposes them to the king through Esther, because the order of preachers shows the faithful, who are members of Christ, that they must beware of their deceits and perversity of heart.

The two eunuchs may also be understood as representing heretics and schismatics, who carry the poison of fraud and malice in their hearts and continually devise wicked counsels against the truth, seeking to remove it from the hearts of believers and, in a certain sense, to kill Christ, who is the life of the faithful, within them. But when the holy teachers expose their wickedness, they bring the hiding places of their errors into the light, showing how the innocent are rescued from the death of the soul by God’s judgment, how the guilty are punished by just retribution, and how those who have done well are rewarded with a fitting recompense.

Therefore it follows:

«The matter was investigated, and it was found to be so; and both were hanged on the gallows. And the king commanded that it be written in the book of records, so that something might be repaid to him for his life; and it was handed down to the histories and annals in the presence of the king.»

The books of records, therefore, are the volumes of the two Testaments, in which it is recorded what rewards await the righteous in the future for good deeds and what punishments await the wicked for sins.

Thus it is written in the Gospel: «The Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father, and then he will repay each according to his works (Matt. XVI).»

And again: «The wicked, he says, will go into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life (Matt. XXV).»

Hence Paul, writing to the Romans, says: «For the wrath of God is revealed against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness; he will repay each according to his works: to those who, through perseverance in good work, seek glory, honor, and incorruption, eternal life; but to those who are contentious and do not obey the truth, but believe in unrighteousness, wrath and indignation. Tribulation and anguish upon every soul that works evil (Rom. I and II).»

Concerning this it is also said through Ezekiel: «The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the impiety of the wicked shall be upon him. The soul that sins shall itself die (Ezek. XVIII).»

The Psalmist likewise bears witness, saying: «The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are attentive to their prayers; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy their memory from the earth (Ps. XXXIII).»

## CHAPTER VI. How, because Mardochai refused to worship him, Haman, hating the Jewish race, accused them to the king, who commanded that they all be killed on one day

«After these things King Ahasuerus exalted Haman, son of Hammedatha, who was of the stock of Agag, and placed his seat above all the princes he had. And all the king’s servants who were in the doors of the palace bent their knees and worshiped Haman, for so the emperor had commanded them; only Mardochai did not bend his knee or worship him.»

What is signified by the proud Haman except the arrogance of the powerful of this age? Abusing the benefits bestowed upon them by divine mercy, they disdain to have as partners in grace those who share their nature. Therefore they wickedly strive to transfer to themselves the honor and reverence that they ought justly to offer to God alone. Those who refuse to do or approve this they pursue with hatred, persecute with torments, and attempt to hand over to death.

But the heavenly Judge «who looks upon the humble and knows the lofty from afar, who knows the deceiver and the one deceived, turns the pain of the wicked back upon their own heads, and their iniquity descends upon their own crowns. The wicked are caught in their own snares; the righteous is delivered from his distress, and the wicked is handed over in his place (Ps. CXII).»

This Haman the Agagite, whom Josephus relates to have been born from the stock of Amalek, may also represent the bloodthirsty Jewish people, who killed the prophets and did not fear killing the Lord himself, the Lord of the prophets, and his apostles. Losing the nobility of their race because of their unbelief and hardness of mind, they were called by Isaiah “rulers of Sodom” and “people of Gomorrah.” To them it is said through Ezekiel: «Your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite (Ezek. XVI).»

These people, therefore, regard the confessors of Christ as though they were enemies of God’s Law. Thus they hasten to lay hands not only upon Mardochai—that is, upon the preachers of the Gospel—but also upon the entire catholic people, and to destroy them from the present life. Yet the death by which they plotted to punish the innocent temporally they themselves, as their merits demanded and the just Judge repaid, are compelled to endure without end in their souls.

«And Haman said to King Ahasuerus: “There is a people scattered throughout all the provinces and separated from one another, using new laws and ceremonies, and moreover disregarding the king’s decrees. You know very well that it is not expedient for your kingdom that they should grow insolent through license. If it pleases you, decree that they perish, and I will weigh ten thousand talents for the treasuries of your wealth.”»

Then the king took the ring he used from his hand and gave it to Haman, son of Hammedatha, of the progeny of Agag, the enemy of the Jews, and said to him: «Let the silver you promise be yours; deal with the people as you please.»

Thus Haman, promising the king ten talents of money, sought the death of the Jews. So also the Jewish people, devoted to the carnal observance of the ceremonies of the Law and believing that by this they were pleasing God, plotted the death of the true confessors of Christ, who offered spiritual service to God according to evangelical teaching.

Therefore, just as Haman took care to send letters sealed with the king’s signet, so that by this means he might more easily accomplish his desire, so the unbelief of the Jews, wrongly taking the books of the divine Law—in which the seal of the supreme King is expressed, that is, the grace of the Holy Spirit made manifest—as testimony to establish its heresy, strove to reject the conversion of the nations into fellowship with the faith and to condemn the Gospel of Christ as though it were contrary to the divine commandments.

Nor is it without a mystery that the twelfth month of the year, which is called Adar, was assigned by lot for the slaughter of Israel; rather, it signifies that the grace of Christ, which was entrusted to the faithful in the fullness of time, will suffer a powerful persecution in the world through the faithful in the last times. Concerning this, the teacher of the nations, writing to Timothy, says:

> “But know this, that in the last times perilous periods will come, and people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked, without affection, without peace, slanderers, incontinent, ruthless, without kindness, traitors, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than of God, having indeed an appearance of piety but denying its power.”

Hence the Lord also says in the Gospel:

> “This Gospel of the kingdom will be preached throughout the whole world, as a testimony to all nations, and then the consummation will come” (Matthew 29).

And shortly afterward:

> “Then,” he says, “there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor will be; unless those days had been shortened” (ibid.).

Immediately the edict was displayed in Susa, “while the king and Haman were celebrating a feast, and all the Jews who were in the city were weeping.” This is what the Savior foretold to his disciples in the Gospel:

> “Amen, amen, I say to you: you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy” (John 16).

Let us therefore see what Scripture next relates about Mordecai.

## CHAPTER VII. On Mordecai’s learning of this, putting on sackcloth and sending to Esther to plead with the king for the death of the Jews. [Col. 0654A]

> “When Mordecai heard this, he tore his garments, put on sackcloth, sprinkled ashes on his head, and in the middle of the city cried out with a loud voice, displaying the bitterness of his spirit; and with this lament he proceeded as far as the doors of the palace. For it was not lawful for anyone dressed in sackcloth to enter the king’s court,” etc.

When Mordecai heard that the death of the Jews had been decreed by imperial edicts, he clothed himself in mourning garments and, in bitterness of spirit and with a lamenting voice, proceeded as far as the palace doors. In the same way, when the teachers of the Church hear of the persecution that the rulers of the earth desire to inflict upon the innocent servants of Christ, they long to pour out their needs in the hidden places of heaven—that is, in the sight of the heavenly Judge—with fasting and almsgiving, with vigils and prayers, with tears and contrition of heart. Thus, through the dignity and prayers of the true queen, namely the holy Church—which partly still journeys on earth, and partly already reigns with the Lord in heaven—they may deserve to be heard by the King of all ages. [Col. 0654B]

If anyone asks how it is fitting for the most just King to inflict torments upon the innocent, let him know that this proceeds not from a desire for malice but from the command of the highest counsel. For divine wisdom, which overcomes all wickedness, reaches mightily from end to end, and orders all things gently; it itself does whatever it wills in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the abysses. It is therefore accomplished by a just judgment that his faithful servants are handed over to persecutors, whether for the expiation of sins, for correction of conduct, or even for the increase of merits and multiplication of rewards, because, as the Prophet testifies:

> “The Lord is just in all his ways and holy in all his works; he is near to all who call upon him” (Psalm 144).

In truth, he will do the will of those who fear him, hear their prayers, and save them. For the Lord did not hand Job over into Satan’s hands at Satan’s request so that he might perish, but so that, with his aid, Job might conquer the most wicked enemy, thus acquiring for himself the palm of victory and leaving the enemy the just punishment for his wickedness. A thorn in his flesh was given to the apostle Paul, namely an angel of Satan, to strike him, so that strength might be perfected in weakness. [Col. 0654D]

Nor should it be passed over in silence that Mordecai is said to have been unable to enter the king’s court while dressed in sackcloth, but to have reached as far as the palace doors. No one can enter the court of the heavenly homeland while still subject to the corruption of the present life. Rather, before the day of his final death, each person ought, through chastisement of the body and contrition of heart, to knock at the entrance of the kingdom, and thus, after departing through death, joyfully enter the Lord’s paradise.

> “Esther therefore sent these words to Mordecai: Go and gather all the Jews whom you find in Susa, and pray for me. Do not eat or drink for three days and three nights. I also, with my maidservants, will fast in the same way, and then I will enter the king, acting against the law, though uninvited.”

Mordecai prays with the Jews for Queen Esther, and likewise the queen herself prays for Mordecai and the Jews, because teachers ought to pour out prayers to the Lord for their disciples, and disciples for their teachers, so that the entire assembly of the faithful together—that is, the members with the whole body—may be kept unharmed by heavenly piety. Hence Paul, writing to the Romans, says that he continually remembers them without ceasing in his prayers; and he likewise begs those same Romans, by the Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Holy Spirit, to assist him in prayers and to pray to the Lord for him, [Col. 0655B] that he may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judaea and that his ministry, which he is carrying to Jerusalem, may be acceptable to the saints. Hence it is also written in the Acts of the Apostles that, when Peter had been placed in prison, the Church prayed for him without ceasing to the Lord. And he himself similarly asks in his Epistle that the grace and peace of God may be multiplied and fulfilled in the Church through the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

## CHAPTER VIII. Esther entered the king and invited him and Haman to a feast. [Col. 0655C]

> “On the third day Esther put on royal garments and stood in the inner court of the royal house, opposite the king’s hall; while he was sitting upon the throne in the audience chamber of the palace, opposite the entrance of the house. When he saw Queen Esther standing there, she pleased his eyes, and he extended toward her the golden scepter that he held in his hand. She approached and kissed the top of his scepter, and the king said to her: What do you wish, Queen Esther, and what is your request? Even if you should ask for half of the kingdom, it will be given to you. She answered: I ask that you come to me today, and Haman with you, to the feast.”

What does it mean that on the third day Esther put on royal garments, except that the Church of the nations, in the third age of the world—that is, after the incarnation, passion, and resurrection of Christ—clothed herself, through confession of the Holy Trinity, in the sacraments of baptism and in the beauty of faith, hope, charity, and every virtue, so that she might thereby become worthy of royal fellowship, while she burned unceasingly with her supreme love?

She stands in the inner court of the royal house, opposite the king’s hall—that is, in the devout activity of the present life, which looks toward the future reward in heaven, where the King of kings himself sits upon his heavenly throne and gives heed to the prayers of those who devoutly cry out to him. He extends the scepter that he holds in his hand toward this queen when he displays to her the power of his rule, or the cross of his passion, through which he acquired power in heaven, on earth, and beneath the earth, so that “at his name every knee should bend, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.” She herself lovingly kisses it—that is, venerates it with complete devotion. [Col. 0656A]

The king himself promises to grant her request, just as he says in the Gospel:

> “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you” (Matthew 7).

And again:

> “Ask,” he says, “and you will receive, so that your joy may be full.”

The full joy of the holy Church is granted nowhere but in the possession of the heavenly kingdom, where the blessed queen will reign forever with Christ the King. After she had been granted the choice of making her request, she invited him to the feast that she had prepared for him. This is best understood as nothing other than the full and perfect devotion of her faith, by which the inward Inspector and Judge of all ages is nourished. To this refreshment—that is, to the communion of sound faith—the Church invites not only her friends but also her enemies and persecutors, namely pagans, Jews, and heretics, so that, abandoning every path of error, they may rejoice together in the common good within the one house of Catholic confession:

> “Immediately the king said: Call Haman, so that he may obey Esther’s wishes. So the king and Haman came to the feast that the queen had prepared for them.”

Observe that the will of the inviting queen and the command of the commanding king agree. But woe to the wicked man who approaches the Lord’s table, who has a heart polluted with hatred and an unclean conscience, and yet does not fear to enter the Lord’s feast unworthily. Although he may have come after being invited many times, his own merits will compel him not to remain in the joy of the banqueters. Rather, when the king enters and sees him reclining there without a wedding garment, he rebukes him for his presumption and, ordering his hands and feet bound, commands him to be cast into the outer darkness, where he will be compelled justly to endure the harm of the deceit that he wickedly prepared for the innocent, according to Solomon’s saying:

> “The wicked will be caught in their own snares.”

After the king had given Esther a second opportunity to make her request, she answered:

> “If I have found favor in the king’s sight, and if it pleases the king to give me what I ask and fulfill my request, let the king and Haman come to the feast that I have prepared for them, and tomorrow I will reveal my desire to the king.”

This delay in making her request is not to be attributed to the fault of sloth but to the virtue of patience. It signifies that reward for the just and punishment for sinners are chiefly to be assigned in the future. Here “tomorrow” is understood as the future time, as in the Gospel saying:

> “Do not be anxious about tomorrow.”

And in Genesis Jacob says to Laban:

> “Tomorrow my righteousness will appear.”

In Exodus, too, where the eating of the paschal lamb is prescribed, it is added:

> “Nothing of it shall remain until morning.”

When the day of the future judgment arrives and the whole human race—both the just and sinners—stands before the presence of the supreme Judge, then it will be revealed with what disposition each person lived here. The just will be invited by the sentence of the present Judge to receive the kingdom of the heavenly homeland, while sinners will be driven away to be punished with the devil by the torments of hell.

## CHAPTER IX. On King Ahasuerus’s spending the night sleepless and ordering the histories and annals of former times to be brought to him; while they were being read before him, they reached the place where Mordecai had exposed the eunuchs who were plotting, after which the king ordered Haman to adorn him with a royal robe and diadem and to have the king’s friend proclaimed while mounted upon the royal horse. Hence Haman returned home sorrowful. [Col. 0657A]

> “That night the king spent sleepless, and he ordered the histories and annals of former times to be brought to him. When these were being read in his presence, they came to the passage where it was written how Mordecai had reported the plot of Bagathan and Thares, the eunuchs who desired to assassinate King Ahasuerus. When the king heard this, he said: What honor and reward did Mordecai receive for this loyalty? His servants and ministers said to him: He received no reward at all. Immediately the king said: Who is in the court? Haman had entered the inner court of the royal house to suggest to the king that Mordecai be hanged on the gallows that had been prepared for him. The servants answered: Haman is standing in the court. The king said: Let him enter. When he had entered, the king said to him: What should be done to the man whom the king desires to honor? Haman, thinking in his heart and supposing that the king wished to honor no one but himself, answered: The man whom the king desires to honor should be clothed in royal garments, placed upon a horse taken from the king’s saddle, receive the royal diadem upon his head, and have one of the king’s princes and tyrants lead his horse at the front. As he proceeds through the city streets, the leader should proclaim: Thus shall the man be honored whom the king wishes to honor. The king said to him: Hurry, take the robe and the horse, and do as you have said to Mordecai the Jew, who sits before the palace doors. Take care to omit nothing of what you have said.”

What does it mean that the king spent the night sleepless, except what is written in the Psalm:

> “Behold, he neither slumbers nor sleeps who guards Israel” (Psalm 120)?

The histories and annals of former times are read before him, containing the record of Mordecai’s faith and good deeds, because the King of the saints and Prince of the kings of the earth, remaining himself unchanged, contemplates the course of all ages and the knowledge of every deed in a single glance. Nothing is past for him; everything lies open, present before his sight. Concerning him Jeremiah says:

> “He who established all things is himself, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance; the Lord of hosts is his name” (Jeremiah 10).

Hence the Apostle also says:

> “In Christ Jesus there is not ‘is and was,’ but there is always ‘is.’”

And again:

> “Jesus Christ,” he says, “is the same yesterday and today and forever.”

Mordecai’s deeds are therefore remembered before this king, because the good works of the holy teachers will never be consigned to oblivion before him. Rather, what is written is fulfilled:

> “The righteous will be in everlasting memory; he will not fear an evil report” (Psalm 111).

[Col. 0658A] Mordecai is ordered to be clothed in royal garments, placed upon a horse taken from the king’s saddle, and to receive the royal diadem upon his head; one of the king’s princes and tyrants is to lead his horse at the front, and, proceeding through the city streets, proclaim:

> “Thus shall the man be honored whom the king wishes to honor.”

So the holy preachers of the Gospel and teachers of the Church, illumined by the adornment of every virtue and by the beauty of wisdom, and honored with the diadem of royal dignity because they are members of the supreme King, are commanded to mount the royal horse—that is, to preside over and rule the faithful people, in whose hearts the King of heaven himself continually dwells. Concerning these horses, the prophet Habakkuk says to the Lord:

> “You will surely mount upon your horses, and your riding is salvation” (Habakkuk 3). [Col. 0658B]

Haman, the spiritual enemy of God’s people, renders him worthy service, though unwillingly, when the persecutors of the holy Church, despite their irreverent disposition, are nevertheless often compelled by heavenly providence to proclaim the Church’s truth by their testimony. Once the truth has been revealed, those who have been confuted cannot conceal what is manifest.

> “Mordecai returned to the palace gate, but Haman hastened to his house mourning and with his head uncovered. He told Zeresh his wife and his friends everything that had happened to him. The wise men whom he had in his council, and his wife, answered him: If Mordecai is of Jewish descent, before whom you have begun to fall, you will not be able to resist him; you will fall before him.”

This is the transformation wrought by the right hand of the Most High: the man who had recently boasted that he was powerful over others and more glorious than all suddenly became lower than the rest and weaker than everyone. Considering the greatness of this arrangement, Mary, the mother of the Lord, says in the Gospel canticle:

> “He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts. He has brought down the powerful from their thrones and exalted the humble. He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty” (Luke 1).

Concerning this Isaiah says:

> “Lebanon will be turned, and Carmel will be reckoned as a forest” (Isaiah 29).

Here we see the obstinacy of the Synagogue of the Jews suppressed and the humility of the Church of the nations exalted. Here the persecutors of the Christian faith, who once tore Christ’s flock like savage lions, have now been destroyed and reduced to nothing; while the confessors of Christ, standing upright throughout the world in the soundness of the faith, have been raised up by the power of their virtues. The head has been turned into the tail and the tail into the head, because:

> “Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

## CHAPTER X. On the second day of the feast, when the queen pleaded for her people, Haman was hanged on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai

> “While they were still speaking, the king’s eunuchs came and quickly compelled him to proceed to the feast that the queen had prepared. The king and Haman entered to drink with the queen. On the second day also, after he had become heated with wine, the king said to her: What is your request, Esther, that it may be granted to you, and what do you wish to be done? Even if you should ask for half my kingdom, you will obtain it. She answered him: If I have found favor in your eyes, O king, and if it pleases you, grant me my life, for which I ask, and my people, for whom I plead. For I and my people have been delivered up to be crushed, slaughtered, and destroyed. If only we had been sold as male and female slaves! The evil would have been tolerable, and I would have remained silent, groaning. But now our enemy is one whose cruelty rebounds upon the king. King Ahasuerus answered and said: Who is he, and of what power is he, that he dares to do this? Esther said: Our worst enemy and adversary is Haman. When he heard this, he was immediately struck with terror, unable to endure the sight of the king and queen.”

Behold, the second day of the feast has arrived. Haman is summoned and comes just as before; but when Esther makes her request known, he withdraws, already condemned to punishment. This is why in the Gospel a meal is mentioned in one place and a dinner in another as prepared by a man: the meal signifies the present Church, while the dinner signifies the eternal and final banquet. Thus sinners are separated, and the good alone rejoice in the sight of their Creator.

Haman, the spiritual enemy and adversary of God’s people, because he did not possess the garment of charity by which he would have been worthy of the royal banquet, felt the king’s anger. While the king hastened into the garden—that is, while he invited his elect to the delights of paradise—Haman attempted to plead with the queen for his life, but in vain, because he found no suitable time for this. It is already too late to seek remedies for salvation when the vengeance of retribution is imminent.

So also in the Gospel parable, when the bridegroom arrives, the foolish virgins ask the prudent for oil with which to replenish their vessels, but do not receive it. After the Bridegroom has entered the wedding with the prudent virgins and the door has been closed, they remain shut out and seek an entrance for themselves. Yet they can in no way obtain it, because they no longer find the time of mercy, which earlier they had neglected to seek through worthy deeds.

There the one who refused here to hear what the Lord commanded cannot now obtain from the Lord what he asks. The person who has wasted the proper time for repentance comes in vain with prayers before the gate of the kingdom. Hence the Lord says through Solomon:

> “I called, and you refused; I stretched out my hand, and there was no one who looked; you disregarded all my counsel and neglected my rebukes. I also will laugh at your destruction and mock you when what you feared comes upon you; when sudden calamity falls upon you and destruction rushes in like a storm, then they will call upon me, and I will not answer; they will rise early, and they will not find me” (Proverbs 1).

> “When the king returned and entered the place of the feast, he found Haman fallen upon the couch on which Esther was lying, and he said: Does he also intend to violate the queen in my presence, in my own house? The word had scarcely gone out of the king’s mouth when they immediately covered his face.”

For Haman’s entreaty to Queen Esther before King Ahasuerus was reckoned as a slanderous act, because when the day of judgment is imminent, the petition of the wicked becomes not prayer but provocation. Hence it is written in the Psalm:

> “When he is judged, let him go forth condemned, and let his prayer become sin” (Psalm 108).

Then the oppression with which they formerly oppressed the humble is charged against them, because the time of recompense has arrived. Then sinners condemned for their sins will be covered with shame, as it is written:

> “The confusion of their faces will cover them,”

when they are dragged into the darkness of Tartarus, there to receive the fitting recompense of their deeds. Hence it follows:

> “Harbona, one of the eunuchs who stood in the king’s service, said: Behold, the gallows that Haman prepared for Mordecai, who spoke on behalf of the king, stands in Haman’s house; it is fifty cubits high. The king said to him: Hang him on it. So Haman was hanged on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king’s anger was quieted.”

It is written in Proverbs:

> “Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone, it will roll back upon him” (Proverbs 26).

So Haman was compelled to endure the cross that he had prepared for Mordecai.

But it may be asked what it signifies that the cross itself is said to have been made fifty cubits high. The Law was given to the former people on Mount Sinai on the fiftieth day after the sacrifice of the lamb. Since we have said above [Col. 0660C] that Haman signified the Jews themselves, who stirred up opposition against Christ—who had been promised to them in the Law—and persecuted his Church, the Law itself, which had been given to them for the preservation of life, became the cause of their death, because through it they sought to extinguish the name of Christ and kill his confessors. Thus those who unjustly desired to oppress the innocent through the Law itself received through it the sentence of a just judgment, concerning which Paul says:

> “All who have sinned under the Law will be judged by the Law” (Romans 2).

Harbona the eunuch, who exposed the cross that had been made, signifies the teachers of the Law, who by reading the Law itself revealed the deceit of the Jews and everything they had done contrary to the divine commandments. Hence Moses, foreseeing in the Spirit that they would become despisers and sacrilegious, foretold in the song of Deuteronomy everything that was to befall the transgressors. Hence the Savior also says to those same Jews in the Gospel:

> “Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father; there is one who accuses you, Moses, in whom you hope. For if you believed Moses, you would perhaps believe me also, for he wrote about me. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?” (John 5).

## CHAPTER XI. On Mordecai’s being appointed in Haman’s place and, at the queen’s request, letters being sent for the salvation of the Jews [Col. 0661A]

> “On that day King Ahasuerus gave to Queen Esther the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews. And Mordecai entered before the face of the king,” etc.

What does it mean that King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews, except that the true King and our Lord, after the former people had despised the coming in the flesh of the Mediator between God and human beings and had refused to receive his Gospel, transferred to the holy Church the whole dignity and honor that the former people had possessed through knowledge of the Law and the prophets and through the practice of devout religion? Thus the Church might possess spiritual riches and become the most honorable guardian of every virtue. Hence it is written in Proverbs:

> “The substance of the sinner is stored up for the righteous” (Proverbs 13).

And the Lord says to those same Jews in the Gospel:

> “The kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruits” (Matthew 21).

Again, through Solomon, it is said:

> “The one who is good will receive favor from the Lord” (Proverbs 12).

Hence it follows concerning Mordecai that he entered before the face of the king, because, while the Church praises and proclaims the zeal of her teachers, those holy teachers themselves, for the labor they have expended in nurturing the faithful, find abundant favor before the sight of the Creator of all.

This statement may also be understood as spoken generally concerning all the persecutors of the Church. Whatever they produced through their pursuit of wisdom or useful disciplines, whatever they investigated in their search for moral excellence, and even whatever they devised in the category of punishments for torturing the martyrs—all of it has been turned to the increase of honor [Col. 0661C] and glory for Christ’s faithful. Nothing of a good reward remained for those unjust possessors in return for their labor; rather, everything was bestowed upon these faithful people for the fullness of their perfection.

What is also added—that the king took the ring which he had received from Haman and gave it to Mordecai—mystically expresses that the seal of faith, which the faithless Jews and all the persecutors of Christ’s name refused to receive when it was offered to them through the preaching of the Gospel, was transferred through Christ’s apostles for the salvation of the nations.

Esther possesses the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews, when the Church of Christ possesses the world, once the enemy of Christians. Mordecai enters before the face of the king when the souls of the saints are daily taken from their dwelling in the present life [Col. 0661D] to contemplate the face of the heavenly Judge. No end occupies the greatness of that joy; rather, their glory continually increases in the joy of eternal rejoicing.

> “Esther appointed Mordecai over her house.”

Behold, Esther appoints Mordecai over her house, because this pleases the holy Church’s wise and salutary counsel: that the multitude of the faithful should be placed under the rule of the holy preachers, so that, through humility and obedience, they may submit themselves to the authority of the chosen teachers.

> “Not content with this, she fell at the king’s feet, wept, and spoke to him, pleading that he order the wickedness of Haman the Agagite and his most evil schemes, which he had devised against the Jews, to be declared void. But he extended toward her, as usual, the golden scepter in his hand, which was shown as a sign of clemency. She rose and stood before him and said: If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his eyes, and if my plea does not seem contrary to him, I ask that by new letters the old letters of Haman, the plotter and enemy of the Jews, by which he had ordered them to perish in all the king’s provinces, be corrected. For how will I be able to endure the death and slaughter of my people? King Ahasuerus answered Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew: I have granted Haman’s house to Esther, and I have ordered him to be hanged on the cross, because he dared to lay his hand upon the Jews. Write therefore to the Jews as you wish, in the king’s name, sealing the letters with my ring.”

What does it mean that Esther falls at the king’s feet and pleads with him for the salvation of her people, except that the holy Church, for the rescue of her children, humbly asks almighty God each day through faith and the mysteries of the incarnation of God’s Only-Begotten Son to restrain by his grace the boldness of her enemies and deliver the innocence of the faithful from their hands?

The heavenly King extends the golden scepter toward the queen who asks, because he powerfully grants her the clemency of his compassion. She asks that the old letters of the most wicked Haman be replaced by new writings, because it is the concern of the true queen that every sect of error and all the hostile schemes that the ancient enemy contrives through his ministers for the destruction of God’s people should be repelled and erased by the most salutary teachings of the Gospel. The letters written in the king’s name are sealed with his ring, because the evangelical doctrine that is preached throughout the world in Christ’s name is everywhere shown to be confirmed by the seal of the Holy Spirit. By the Spirit’s gift, its preachers are filled with everlasting strength, appear unconquerable to all, and remain glorious triumphers over their enemies.

> “It was the time of the third month, which is called Siban. On its twenty-third day letters were written, as Mordecai had commanded, to the Jews and to the rulers, procurators, and judges who governed the one hundred twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia—province to province and people to people, according to their letters and languages—and to the Jews in a form they could read and hear. The letters sent in the king’s name were sealed with his ring and dispatched by mounted couriers, who ran through all the provinces to forestall the former letters with the new messages.”

The month Siban, which among the Hebrews is third in order after Nisan—that is, the month called *Thessari* [Greek: Θεσσαρί] by the Greeks and June by the Latins—had its twenty-third day when the new letters were written according to Mordecai’s dictation, to refute Haman’s former letters.

The meaning of this is evident: the doctrine of the Gospel was established by the writers of the New Testament through our Lord Jesus Christ in such a way that the faith of the Holy Trinity was fully embraced in it, and the complete perfection of the entire Decalogue was shown to consist in the two commandments of charity. This Scripture was sent through mounted couriers—that is, through holy preachers—throughout the whole world. The one hundred twenty-seven provinces that existed in Ahasuerus’s kingdom signify this. For the number ten, multiplied by twelve, makes one hundred twenty; when seven is added to it, the total concludes the fullness of the whole.

Thus the true observance of the Decalogue was communicated by apostolic tradition through holy teachers to every part of the world, while the grace of the sevenfold Spirit was poured into the hearts of the faithful. Nor is it without a mystery that the letters sent in the king’s name and sealed with his ring are said to have been written according to the letters and languages of each nation, so that every nation could read and understand them. The doctrine of the Gospel was ordered in this way: its first teachers, instructed by the grace of the Holy Spirit, initially spoke in the languages of all peoples; then, through their ministry, the word of faith was sown throughout every part of the world. Thus it is read in the Acts of the Apostles that in the upper room of Zion, on the day of Pentecost, the Paraclete Spirit came upon the one hundred twenty believers in the form of fire and enabled them to speak of the mighty works of God in the languages of all nations, so that all who had gathered and heard this marveled in astonishment.

[Col. 0663C]

> “The king commanded them to assemble the Jews in each city and order them to gather together in one place, so that they might stand for their lives and kill all their enemies, together with their wives, children, and entire households. One day of vengeance was established throughout all the provinces, namely the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar. The substance of the letter was that in all the lands and among all the peoples subject to the authority of King Ahasuerus, it should be made known that the Jews were ready to take vengeance upon their enemies.”

What does it mean that this earthly king commands his mounted couriers to assemble the Jews in every place and order them to gather together so that they might stand for their lives and kill all their enemies, together with their wives and children and entire households, except that our King, the ruler of heaven and earth, commands this through his preachers to the true Jews and his confessors among all nations: they are to gather into the unity of fellowship and peace and fight for the salvation of their souls. They are to condemn all their enemies, both visible and invisible—that is, the false Jews, who are the synagogue of Satan, pagans, incorrigible heretics, and unclean spirits, together with all impieties and wicked inventions—and leave nothing of these things remaining. Indeed, they are to extinguish entirely their wives and children—that is, carnal pleasure and the works of sin—together with their households, namely worldly ambition, and permit nothing that could harm them to remain from these things.

Hence the Lord commanded the Israelites in the Law to kill and destroy the nations opposed to them in the promised land. Hence he later commanded the Amalekites to be destroyed to the point of annihilation, because he desired to remove from them every occasion of stumbling. Remembering this, the prophet says in the Psalms:

> “In the mornings I killed all the sinners of the land, so that I might destroy from the city of the Lord all who work iniquity” (Psalm 100).

Moreover, the time appointed for this slaughter of the enemies aptly accords with the mystery of this spiritual destruction. The twelfth month of the Hebrews, namely Adar, expresses only the final age of the world, in which this spiritual battle is waged most intensely by Christ’s soldiers. Likewise, the thirteenth day signifies the faith of the Holy Trinity together with observance of God’s commandments, through which all adversaries are rightly conquered.

What is added, namely:

> “And the king’s edict was displayed in Susa,”

signifies that the authority of the heavenly King stands supreme and rules throughout the whole world:

> “All things have been placed under his dominion, and no one can resist his will” (Esther 13),

and worldly arrogance lies prostrate beneath his power. Hence it is rightly said that the king’s edict was also displayed in Susa, for *Susa* is interpreted as “riding” or “reporting.” In the end, the pride of the world is overcome by the power of God. Hence the Savior says to his disciples in the Gospel:

> “In the world you will have distress, but take courage, because I have conquered the world” [Col. 0664C] (John 16).

## CHAPTER XII. On Mordecai’s glory, how the Jews took vengeance on their enemies, and the hanging of Haman’s ten sons on the gallows
“Now Mordecai, leaving the palace and the king’s presence, shone in royal garments—namely, violet and sky-blue ones—wearing a golden crown on his head and wrapped in a silken and purple cloak; and the whole city rejoiced and was glad.”

Great is the glory of the holy teachers when, through their doctrine and exhortation, the faithful overcome the savagery of the most wicked enemy by the power of the heavenly King. Their reward therefore remains in the heavenly kingdom of eternal blessedness and perpetual brightness, which the color of hyacinth and the splendor of gold seem to symbolize. For the martyrs of Christ, because of the shedding of their blood, royal dignity is bestowed by the most just Rewarder, so that they may reign together with Christ the King in the heavenly citadel. The names of purple and silk prefigure this reality, and the entire assembly of the saints will likewise rejoice and be glad on account of it in the heavenly Jerusalem. Concerning this it follows:

“Now a new light seemed to arise for the Jews: joy, honor, and triumph. Among all peoples, cities, and provinces, wherever the king’s commands arrived, there was extraordinary rejoicing, feasting, banquets, and a festival day, so much so that many of another nation and sect joined their religion and ceremonies. For a great terror of the Jewish name had seized everyone.”

Accordingly, very many from among the Gentiles and the enemies of the Church, impressed by the number, strength, wisdom, and steadfastness of the holy martyrs and by the power of Christ shining forth through them, abandoned idolatry and pagan superstition and were converted to the Christian religion. This is by no means hidden from those who read the sufferings of the saints and the triumphs of the martyrs; and through God’s mercy the number of the faithful increases daily and the enclosures of the Church are filled. For the vigor of the Christian name arouses terror among unbelievers throughout the whole world and joy among believers. Concerning this the Psalmist says: “Let all the earth fear the Lord; and let all who inhabit the world be moved by him” (Ps. XXXII). And again: “The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him, and all the upright in heart will be praised” (Ps. LXIII). The Apostle likewise says: “At the name of Jesus every knee shall bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth, and every tongue shall confess that the Lord Jesus is in the glory of God the Father” (Phil. II).

“Accordingly, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which we have already said is called Adar, when slaughter had been prepared for all the Jews and their enemies were thirsting for their blood, the situation was reversed: the Jews began to prevail and to avenge themselves upon their adversaries. They gathered together in each city, town, and locality in order to stretch out their hands against their enemies and persecutors, and no one dared to resist them, because dread of their greatness had penetrated all the peoples.”

As stated above, the twelfth month signifies the final age of the world, when the Redeemer was incarnate and the preaching of his Gospel was spread throughout the whole world. Likewise, the thirteenth day declares the light of faith and of good works, which is daily brought to completion in the Church among the faithful through evangelical preaching. For in the twelfth month, “on the thirteenth day of the month, when slaughter had been prepared for all the Jews and their enemies were thirsting for their blood, the Jews themselves began to prevail and to avenge themselves upon their adversaries”; because the assembly of the faithful, in which there is the true confession of orthodox faith, although the enemies and persecutors of Christ’s name everywhere stir up persecutions against them and strive to oppress them, nevertheless, aided by God’s grace and strengthened by the shield of faith and the armor of righteousness, overcomes its adversaries and carries away from them the trophy of glory. It does this when, having driven back the spiritual wickednesses and the sowers of error who were seducing them through various vices, it converts them to the light of faith and makes them participants in Christ’s grace.

“And no one dared to resist them.” For the fear of the divine majesty, which is revealed in the Church through shining miracles, strongly shakes the hearts of the carnal and compels them to yield to the word of God. Concerning this it appropriately follows:

“For the judges of the provinces, the leaders and governors, and every authority that presided over the several places and offices, exalted the Jews because of their fear of Mordecai, whom they knew to be the chief officer of the palace and to possess very great power; and the fame of his name increased daily and flew through everyone’s mouth.”

For the praiseworthy conduct and the power of the virtues of the holy teachers grant great honor and reverence to the multitude of the faithful. Hence, in the Acts of the Apostles, where those first preachers of the Gospel are said to have devoted themselves to the doctrine of God’s word and to healing, it is written: “They were persevering in the apostles’ teaching, in fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers. Fear came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were performed through the apostles in Jerusalem; and great fear was upon all” (Acts II). And again: “By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were performed among the people, and they were all together in Solomon’s portico. But none of the others dared to join them; nevertheless, the people magnified them” (Acts V).

“Accordingly, the Jews struck their enemies with a great blow and killed them, repaying them for what they had prepared to do to them, so that even in Susa they killed five hundred men, apart from the ten sons of Haman the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.”

What is meant by the fact that the Jews are said to have killed five hundred men in Susa while pursuing their enemies, excepting the ten sons of Haman whom they fastened to gallows? It means that not only among the nations do all workers of iniquity who persist in their wickedness, refuse to repent of their sins, and do not take care to receive remission of their offenses through the grace of the Holy Spirit appear detestable and worthy of condemnation to the people of God; but also the carnal Jews themselves—namely, transgressors of the Decalogue of the Mosaic Law—will justly be compelled to endure the punishment of hell because of the guilt of Christ’s cross, which by their faithlessness they incurred for themselves in his Passion. None of the number of the elect deigns to share in their wickedness or imitate their evil deeds. Hence it is rightly added that, after the Jews had killed their enemies, they refused to touch or take anything from their possessions.

“Immediately the number of those who had been killed in Susa was reported to the king, who said to the queen: ‘In the city of Susa the Jews have killed five hundred men and another ten sons of Haman. How much more, do you think, have they slaughtered throughout all the provinces? What more do you ask, and what do you wish me to order to be done?’ She answered him: ‘If it pleases the king, let authority be given to the Jews that, just as they have done today in Susa, so they may do tomorrow also, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows.’ And the king commanded that it be so done,” and so forth.

This intention of Queen Esther, by which she strives vigorously to pursue and eradicate her enemies, expresses the zeal and diligence of the true queen, namely, the holy Church, which pursues her enemies without ceasing and strives to overthrow them utterly and subject them to herself. Through the Psalmist’s voice she says: “I will pursue my enemies and overtake them, and I will not turn back until they fail; I will crush them, and they will not be able to stand” (Ps. XVII).

First she killed five hundred men in Susa, and afterward three hundred, because she shows that not only those who refuse to repent of their sins, but also those who neglect to adorn the faith of the Holy Trinity with good works, are worthy of eternal death. Hence it happened that, just as the Jews killed seventy-five thousand enemies in two days, so through the persistence and effort of the faithful all those enemies who, devoted to the five bodily senses and thinking carnally, refuse through the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit to understand spiritually the law of God, full and perfect in spiritual doctrine, are truly overcome and cast down by the brilliance of the two Testaments. Yet no one wishes to touch anything of their possessions, because the election of the faithful in no way consents to mingle with the wickedness of the lost; rather, in every way it makes itself alien and estranged from their false doctrines and wicked works.

## CHAPTER XIII  
### That the days on which the Jews avenged themselves were counted among the solemn festivals

“Now the thirteenth day of Adar was, among all of them, a day of slaughter, and on the fourteenth day they ceased killing. They appointed it as a festival, so that thereafter they might devote that time to feasting, joy, and banquets. But those who carried out the slaughter in the city of Susa spent the thirteenth and fourteenth days of the same month engaged in slaughter; on the fifteenth day they ceased striking, and therefore appointed that same day as a festival of feasting and rejoicing. But those Jews who lived in unwalled towns and villages decreed the fourteenth day of the month of Adar to be a day of banquets and joy, so that they might rejoice in it and send one another portions of feasts and food.”

What does Scripture mean when it relates that some Jews carried out the slaughter of their enemies on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, ceased killing on the fourteenth day, and held that day as a festival, while others spent two days—namely, the thirteenth and fourteenth days of the aforementioned month—killing their enemies and finally rested solemnly from slaughter on the fifteenth day? It means that some of the saints, after completing the labors which they fulfilled by believing rightly and living well in God’s service, already possess in their hands, before the time of the universal judgment, the Sabbath-rest of eternal repose; while others, remaining in the flesh until the final day of resurrection, after all their enemies have been overcome, are suddenly transformed by divine power and receive eternal rest and blessed immortality, both in their souls and in their bodies, according to what the Apostle says when writing to the Corinthians: “Behold, I tell you a mystery: We shall all indeed rise, but we shall not all be changed. In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet—for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise incorruptible, and we shall be changed” (I Cor. XVI). And to the Thessalonians: “For this we say to you by the word of the Lord: We shall not precede those who have fallen asleep, because the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God; and the dead who are in Christ will rise first. Then we who are alive, who remain, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord” (I Thess. IV).

For the number fourteen, which contains seven twice, signifies the repose of souls from every labor and anxiety. Fifteen, however, in which seven and eight are contained together, prefigures the future rest and immortality of both souls and bodies. Thus the multitude of the elect, after completing the labors of the present life and receiving victory over all enemies, will rejoice in the heavenly kingdom with eternal exultation and mutual love. There will be no end to this joy, because no further sorrow of labor follows it. The diligence of the holy preachers commends this to their hearers as something to be believed and understood. Hence it is added:

“Therefore Mordecai wrote all these things and sent them in a letter to the Jews who lived in all the provinces of the king, both near and far, so that they might accept the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar as festivals and, as each year returned, celebrate them with solemn honor. For on those days the Jews had avenged themselves upon their enemies, and mourning and sorrow had been changed into gladness and joy; and these days were to be days of feasting and rejoicing, when they would send one another portions of food and distribute small gifts to the poor. And the Jews accepted as a solemn observance everything that they had begun to do at that time and that Mordecai had commanded by letter to be done.”

For all the faithful continually strive through pious labor, good works, and the distribution of alms to attain, according to the teaching of the Gospel and the Apostles, the entrance into eternal life through faith, hope, and love. They strive also to strengthen both themselves and those who serve them by comforting them amid the hardship of the present age, so that they may rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all things, and commend their struggle to the faithful Lord in pious prayers, so that through his help they may be rewarded with eternal blessedness.

“For Haman, son of Hammedatha, of the stock of Agag, the enemy and adversary of the Jews, devised evil against them in order to kill and destroy them, and cast pur, which in our language is translated as ‘lot.’ Afterward Esther entered the king’s presence, entreating that his efforts might be annulled by the king’s letters and that the evil which he had devised against the Jews might return upon his own head. Finally, both he and his sons were fastened to the cross. From that time these days were called Purim, that is, ‘of lots,’ because pur, that is, the lot, had been cast into the urn.”

For often a wicked person’s desire reaches its fulfillment in a way other than he had hoped, and they themselves become bound in the snare which they set for deceiving others, as Scripture shows, saying: “The wicked will be caught in their own ambushes. And whoever digs a pit will fall into it” (Prov. XI). Thus Haman, who prefigures the enemies of the Church, was compelled to suffer himself the death which he had prepared for Mordecai.

The lot cast into the urn signifies the disposition of any matter in the human mind; yet its outcome depends upon divine judgment. Hence Solomon says: “Lots are cast into the lap, but they are directed by the Lord. For a person’s way is not in his own power; it belongs neither to the one who wills nor to the one who runs, but to God who shows mercy. For all things obey his command, and whatever he wishes he does in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the abysses” (Prov. XVI). How, then, these days of lots ought to be kept in memory by later generations, Scripture shows, saying:

“The Jews took upon themselves and upon their offspring, and upon all who wished to join their religion, that no one should be permitted to pass these two days without solemn observance. Scripture records this, and they are required at fixed times in years continually succeeding one another. These are the days which no forgetfulness will ever erase, and throughout every generation all the provinces of the whole world will celebrate them. There is no city in which the days of Purim, that is, of lots, are not observed by the Jews and by their descendants, who are bound to these ceremonies.”

Therefore the days of lots, on which God grants his true confessors victory over their enemies, must never be erased by forgetfulness, but must be celebrated throughout every generation in the whole world, because the firm hope of the future repose of souls and the resurrection of bodies on the day of judgment must always be held in remembrance among all the faithful. No Church of Christ throughout the world should be without this observance. Rather, always mindful of this most salutary rite, it should continually prepare itself and conform itself to the reception of future blessings, so that what it celebrates here temporally it may possess there perpetually in the reality of the matter and in eternal blessedness.

Meanwhile, while we are in this pilgrimage, the diligence of the teachers and the Church’s earnest care, following the example of Esther and Mordecai, ought to work with us in teaching and exhortation, so that we may always be devoted to celebrating and honoring this observance. Concerning this it follows:

“Esther the queen, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai also wrote a second letter, so that this festival day might thereafter be established with every diligence. They sent it to all the Jews who lived in the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces of King Ahasuerus, so that they might have peace and receive the truth, observing the days of lots and celebrating them with joy at their appointed time, just as Mordecai and Esther had established. And they accepted for observance, for themselves and their offspring, fasts and cries, the days of lots, and everything contained in the history of this book, which is called Esther.”

This admonition is necessary for us, so that we may always have Christian peace in our hearts and receive the truth of the Gospel, lest through discord and dissension we fall into the error of heretics, where there is no true salvation but certain condemnation and ruin. Hence all who recognize that, through the Church and the ministry of the holy teachers, they have been regenerated in baptism as children of God the Father through the seed of the word of God must without doubt fast piously—that is, lead a pious, chaste, and continent life—raise the cries of their prayers and teachings, and reverently and with firm hope celebrate the days of lots, that is, of the future victory. They must observe with sound faith and good works everything contained in the book of the two Testaments.

## CHAPTER XIV  
### That King Ahasuerus made all the islands tributary; here the history of Esther among the Hebrews ends

“King Ahasuerus made the whole land and all the islands of the sea tributary. His strength, power, dignity, and majesty, by which he exalted Mordecai, are written in the books of the Medes and Persians, as is also how Mordecai, of Jewish descent, was second to King Ahasuerus, great among the Jews and acceptable to the multitude of his brothers, seeking the welfare of his people and speaking what concerned the peace of his offspring.”

What does it mean when it says that King Ahasuerus made the whole land and all the islands of the sea tributary? The historical king of the Persians and Medes never held the whole land under his power, nor could he make all the islands of the sea tributary, since knowledge even of his name could scarcely have reached those islands and regions of the world mentioned above. Rather, this statement more truly expresses our King and Lord Christ, whose power is in heaven, on earth, in the sea, and in all the abysses. He called himself the door in the Gospel, because through him we have entrance into eternal life. According to the testimony of the Psalmist, “All the kings of the earth will worship him”; and to him “all the kings of the earth will serve; the kings of Tharsis and the islands will offer gifts, and the kings of Arabia and Sheba will bring presents” (Ps. LXXI).

The strength, power, dignity, and majesty of this King, and how he exalted the true Mordecai—that is, the assembly of the holy teachers and masters of the Church—before the Christian people, are testified not only by the voices and writings of the one Jewish nation but also by those of all nations. From the beginning he exalted his chosen ones through the gift of his grace and made them glorious and honorable in the sight of all peoples. They seek the welfare of their people and speak what concerns the peace of their offspring, because, according to Isaiah’s prophecy, “The watchmen of the Lord have lifted up their voice; together they will praise” (Isa. LII), and “how beautiful are the feet of those who proclaim peace, who proclaim good things” (Rom. X). For they always ask for the things that concern the peace of Jerusalem, and their offspring will be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples. All who see them will recognize them, because they are the offspring whom the Lord has blessed.

[Col. 0671]

## (A.D. 840)  
### Three Books of Commentaries on the Book of Wisdom by Blessed Rabanus Maurus, Abbot of Fulda and Archbishop of Mainz

## Prologue to Otgar, Archbishop of Mainz

To the most reverend lord, a holy man to be honored with the purest devotion of sincere love and most worthy of every honor, Otgar, archbishop, Rabanus sends greetings in Christ.

Whenever I contemplate your presence, most blessed Father, I am always refreshed by a sweet delight, recalling the gentleness and humility, moderation and temperance that especially flourish in your holiness, so that you are truly recognized as an imitator of the one who commanded his disciples, saying: “Learn from me, because I am meek and humble in heart.” Hence, too, very many, stirred by holy love, have hastened to the service of your veneration and desire with devoted minds to offer whatever service they can.

For this reason, although I do not possess the wealth of earthly things—since I possess only those things that pertain to relieving the needs of Christ’s holy poor—nevertheless, what I have received through divine grace I have decided to add as a small gift, with willing generosity, to the sacred riches that you abundantly possess in the wisdom and knowledge of divine law. I greatly desire that whenever it is presented to your sacred presence, you may remember me, and that, if you find anything useful in it, you may deign to adapt it for the use both of yourself and of your people.

The gift of which I speak is this present volume, which I have recently published as an exposition of the Book of Wisdom, a book that many inscribe with Solomon’s name. Blessed Jerome, however, asserts that it was written not by Solomon, as tradition commonly holds, but by Philo, a most learned Jew; he designated it pseudepigraphal because it appropriates the name of another. The presbyter Bellator testified that he had undertaken an exposition of this volume in eight books. Father Augustine and Saint Ambrose also said certain things about it under the title of homilies.

The diction of this book is exceedingly sweet and truly resplendent with the dignity of its name, and it is most useful for instructing the Church of God. Nevertheless, the aforementioned interpreter of divine law, Jerome, says that this same book is nowhere possessed among the Hebrews, but rather breathes Greek eloquence, and that among the ancients it was not received among the canonical Scriptures, just like the books of Judith, Tobit, and Maccabees. In our own time, however, the holy Church numbers these among the sacred Scriptures and reads them publicly like the other canonical Scriptures; orthodox teachers also frequently use their statements in their doctrines.

The reason why I undertook the labor of expounding this book was that I had found no exposition of the whole work, although the aforementioned presbyter Bellator mentions, as I said, that he produced eight books on it; these, however, have not reached us. I have compressed my own work into three little books so that I might offer the eager reader some understanding of the mysteries of the aforementioned book, reserving more perfect treatments for more perfect readers.

You, most religious priest of Christ, make use of the gift bestowed upon you by your devoted servant. If you find anything pleasing in it, ascribe it solely to God’s gift; but if anything is blameworthy, attribute it rather to my ignorance and weakness than to malice, and do not delay to send me word how it should be corrected. Also support my weakness with prayers before the divine mercy, so that, since he has already granted the will and in some way the beginning, he himself may grant that all things be completed according to his will.

Nor do I think I should conceal from your reverence that I have another work in hand, namely, an exposition of the Book of Ecclesiasticus, which they call Jesus son of Sirach, and which contains many mysteries concerning Christ and the Church. When, with the Lord’s will, I have brought this also to completion, if the present gift has first been gratefully accepted by your holiness, I shall soon endeavor to send it to you with a willing mind.

May the holy God, the Trinity and undivided Unity, deign to preserve your love unharmed and undefiled forever. Holy Father, remember us.

# BOOK ONE

[Col. 0673]

## CHAPTER ONE  
### Wisdom, which is Christ, commands the inhabitants of the earth to love righteousness, teaching them that perverse thoughts separate one from God and that wisdom will not enter a malevolent soul

“Love righteousness, you who judge the earth” (Wis. I). Divine Wisdom admonishes the rulers of God’s people, to whom the power of judging has been given, to love righteousness and preserve equity in judgment.

Alternatively, this statement can generally apply to all who are endowed with reason and possess an understanding mind, so that, judging the earth—that is, their own flesh—they may love righteousness. They should not make provision for the flesh in its desires, but, subjecting it to the command of the spirit, devote themselves above all to the virtues by which the soul is nourished. Then they should care for their body according to necessity, not according to pleasure, always recalling that statement of the Law: “Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God” (Luke IV). They should also remember the Gospel testimony by which the Savior taught his disciples, saying: “Therefore do not be anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’ For the Gentiles seek all these things. Your Father knows that you need all these things. Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you” (Matt. VI).

“Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart.” One thinks of the Lord in goodness when one reads and understands sacred Scripture according to piety; one seeks him in simplicity of heart when one humbly subjects oneself to his will, namely, to keep his commandments. For whoever seeks the Lord piously honors sacred Scripture, does not criticize what he does not yet understand, and therefore does not resist it. This is what it means to be meek, concerning which Truth itself says in the Gospel: “Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth” (Matt. V).

Therefore the philosophers of this world and their followers, the heretics, are excluded—those who think that they can grasp divine secrets by human reason, although it is written: “Who will investigate the wisdom of God that precedes all things?” And the Apostle plainly says that God’s judgments are incomprehensible and his ways unsearchable. In the present life he is to be worshiped through right faith rather than reckless disputation. Hence it follows:

“For he is found by those who do not test him, and he appears to those who have faith in him.” It is dangerous to test God through human presumption, since it is written: “You shall not test the Lord your God.” But it is salutary to honor him with right faith, because “the righteous lives by faith.”

“For perverse thoughts separate from God, but tested virtue rebukes the foolish.” It is clear that every impious thought and depraved will are in no way joined to the Lord or in harmony with the highest good, because “there is no fellowship between light and darkness,” nor any agreement between Christ and Belial. But wherever devotion to and pursuit of sacred virtues are present in a pious heart, they continually reject and condemn the vices and errors of the foolish. Therefore lovers of true wisdom must cleanse their hearts and turn the whole intention of their mind toward love of their Creator.

“For wisdom will not enter a malevolent soul, nor will it dwell in a body subject to sins.” The apostle James, expressing the same thought in his Epistle, wrote: “Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce olives, or a vine figs? So neither can salt water make water sweet. Who is wise and disciplined among you? Let him show his good conduct in the gentleness of wisdom. But if you have bitter jealousy and contentions in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth. This is not the wisdom descending from above, from the Father of lights, but earthly, natural, demonic. For where jealousy and contention are, there is instability and every evil work. But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, moderate, persuadable, consenting to what is good, full of mercy and good fruits, judging without hypocrisy. The fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace” (James III).

True wisdom does not enter a malevolent mind, nor can it dwell in a criminal person. Therefore the philosophers of the Gentiles flatter themselves in vain, as do all heretics and also false Christians, who imagine that they can receive the wisdom of God with a filthy mind and a wicked manner of life. Only those who are pure in heart deserve to receive it as a gift of the Holy Spirit.

## CHAPTER II  
### Wisdom declares that the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee deceit, that he fills the world, and that nothing can be hidden from him

“For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee deceit and withdraw from thoughts that are without understanding.” Hence it is completely clear that Manichaeus, Arius, Eunomius, and the other heretics established their doctrines, full of error, without the grace of the Holy Spirit. For the Spirit of the Lord, being good, always leads into the right way; but the evil spirit leads astray and drags his followers with him into the snare of eternal destruction. Concerning this it follows:

“And he will be rebuked by the iniquity that comes upon him.” For when the time of retribution arrives, all the impious and sinners will receive punishment for their iniquities.

“For the spirit of wisdom is benevolent and will not acquit one who curses with his lips, because the Lord is a witness to his inward parts, a true examiner of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.”

This statement destroys the error of those who think that, just as good thoughts are certainly inspired in us by God, so evil thoughts are generated in our minds at his instigation. Yet God, who is supremely good, desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth, and imposes on no one any necessity of an evil word or wicked deed by which that person might perish. The apostle James shows this, saying: “Let no one, when he is tempted, say, ‘I am tempted by God’; for God is not a tempter of evils, and he himself tempts no one” (James I).

It is as though he said: When someone has committed robbery, theft, false testimony, murder, adultery, or anything of this kind, let him not say, “I had to commit these acts because God compelled me,” and therefore was in no way able to avoid carrying them out. God is not the tempter of evils—that is, of temptations; he himself tempts no one with the temptation that deceives the wretched and causes them to sin.

There are two kinds of temptation: one that deceives and another that tests. According to the kind that deceives, God tempts no one; according to the kind that tests, God tested Abraham. Concerning this the Prophet asks: “Test me, Lord, and tempt me” (Ps. XXV). Each person, however, is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own desire—drawn away from the right path and enticed toward evil. Yet by God’s just judgment the one who refused to obey the Spirit of truth is permitted to fall into it.

“For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the world.” The Holy Spirit, who at the beginning of creation was borne invisibly over the waters by his power, fills and contains every creature by his majesty. Alternatively, by the gift of his power he fills the world of the Church, in which he daily displays the abundance of his beneficence. Hence it follows:

“And he who contains all things has knowledge of the voice.” For, as Paul says:

“To one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit; to another faith in the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing in one Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the discernment of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of words. One and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing them individually as he wills” (I Cor. XII).

“Therefore one who speaks iniquity cannot remain hidden, nor will the judgment that rebukes him pass him by.” For just as the elect receive the gift of knowledge and piety through the grace of the Holy Spirit, so heretics and all the reprobate, inflated by their own pride and stirred up by the evil spirit, cannot hide from God’s Spirit the wickedness of their error, which they shamelessly proclaim; consequently, they cannot escape the vengeance of just punishment.

For just as “the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous and his ears are attentive to their prayers,” so “the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy their memory from the earth.” The Lord questions both the righteous and the wicked; but whoever loves iniquity hates his own soul. Concerning this it follows:

“For the thoughts of the wicked will be examined, and the hearing of his words will come before the Lord, for the correction of his iniquities. For the ear of heaven hears all things, and the tumult of murmuring will not be hidden.”

The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah, having multiplied, came before the Lord, and he came down to see whether they had completed in deed the cry that had reached him. Thus the Lord rained sulfur and fire upon the sinners, from the Lord, and overthrew those cities and the whole surrounding region. In the same way the murmuring of the children of Israel rose up to the Lord, and behold, the Lord’s anger was stirred against the people, and he struck them with an exceedingly great plague. For the Lord God is a consuming fire, a jealous God, and he will repay each person according to his works. Therefore Wisdom necessarily admonishes us, saying:

## CHAPTER III  
### Wisdom commands its hearers to guard themselves from murmuring, detraction, and falsehood, because righteousness is immortal and the impious will not obtain it
Guard yourselves, therefore, from murmuring, which profits nothing, and spare your tongue from detraction, since an obscure answer will not go into the void. How pernicious murmuring and detraction are can be demonstrated by many statements of the sacred Scriptures and by examples of the Lord’s judgments, especially since the Lord himself is often found to have sent punishment upon murmurers and complainers [Col. 0676C]. Scripture says that every mocker is an abomination to the Lord (Prov. III). The Apostle also says that whisperers and detractors are hateful to God (Rom. I). Hence the Psalmist says: “The one who secretly slanders his neighbor, him I pursued.” Elsewhere too we read: “Whoever slanders anyone binds himself for the future”; and, “As a serpent bites in silence, so does one who secretly slanders his brother.” “Death and life are in the power of the tongue.” “The one who is perverse of heart finds no good, and whoever twists his tongue falls into evil.” It is rightly said that an obscure answer will not go into the void, because it will be reserved for the Lord’s judgment. Hence there is that sentence of the Lord: “For every idle word that people speak, they will give an account of it on the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, [Col. 0676D] and by your words you will be condemned.” Concerning this it is also said:

“But the mouth that lies kills the soul.” A lying mouth therefore kills the soul of the liar himself, because it pierces it with the sword of sin. Hence every lie must be avoided with the utmost care, although sometimes a certain kind of lie may be a lighter fault, if someone lies while conferring a benefit. The father Augustine clearly explains this in his book *On Lying*, mentioning that there are eight kinds of lies; whoever wishes may find there how he discussed them. But whoever thinks that some kind of lie is not sin shamefully deceives himself when he supposes himself an honest deceiver of others. [Col. 0677A] Therefore, when examples of lying are set before us from the sacred Scriptures, either they are not lies but are thought to be so because they are not understood, or, if they are lies, they are not to be imitated, since they cannot be just. The statement that God did well by the Hebrew midwives and by Rahab, the prostitute of Jericho, does not mean that he did so because they lied, but because they showed mercy toward God’s people. It was not deceit that was rewarded in them, but benevolence; kindness of mind, not the wickedness of the liar.
